Status Phase 1 of this task was completed Phase 2 is under finalization. Phase 1. The company Algorus Consulting was selected through a competitive process to carry out this assignment in September 2019. Two missions in Ukraine were carried out in November and December 2019 allowing the consultants to present the proposed approach to NEURC receive comments and meet key stakeholders representatives of different DSOs gas traders GTSO etc.. On this basis the consultant was able to continue the work and produced draft deliverables mainly covering the scope of work under the ToR e.g. review of existing metering and billing system in gas distribution review of metering and settlement regulations review the existing consumer categories and reference groups etc.. However starting March 2020 all missions were postponed due to COVID19 pandemic and only limited feedback and comments were received from NEURC until November 2020 with planned meetings being rescheduled due to unavailability of counterparts being on sick leave. The Draft Final Report was prepared by Algorus in August 2020 and delivered in November 2020 due to further absence of key NEURC members. Based on the comments and suggestions provided on the Report there was a need identified further continue the work and partially revise it to fully cover the request and comments presented by the Regulator. For this reason Phase 1 contract with Algorus was closed and considered to be accepted upon inviting a group of experts ready to follow up on methodological recommendations provided by Algorus and convert them into practical elements of daily balancing systems in DSOs. NEURC comments and additional demands were converted into new ToR and the new contract was signed September 2021. Part 2. The group of Ukrainian experts were hired to convert methodological recommendations provided by Algorus and turn them into technical consistent methodology for forecasting the daily consumption of natural gas in the absence of daily data transmission systems further work on mathematical apparatus taking into consideration available data from smart meters of available gas consumers. Considering the fact that the number of smart systems has been significantly increased during the past several years it was decided to update the statistics to further build the mathematical model then based on the proposed mathematical model and using received statistical data on daily consumption to form specify the profiles of consumption develop algorithms for adjusting consumption profiles during operation on the basis of operational dispatch data from smart systems of consumer control groups and determine the dependence of the necessary investments on the required forecasting error for each profile. The first draft of the report was delivered to NEURC at the end of October and fully accepted the final report is expected to be ready March 30 2022.The methodology for forecasting the daily gas consumption was improved considering i availability of daily data on gas consumption from smart meters and daily average air temperature ii significant contamination of input data irregular collection of information failure of meters etc. iii profiles iv the need to ensure the marginal level of forecasting error for 2 days within 10. It was also envisaged to use parametric submodels for forecasting time series data regression models and gradient boosting models and a complex of deep indepth learning models. Now the algorithm for forecasting daily level of natural gas consumption includes the following stages collection and generalization of primary data data cleaning and preparation for analysis and forecasting conducting evaluations of the effectiveness of forecasts based on neural networks selection of the best model based on the methodology forecast. NEURC accepted preliminary results finalization of teh report is ongoing

Status Phase 1 of this task was completed Phase 2 is under finalization. Phase 1. The company Algorus Consulting was selected through a competitive process to carry out this assignment in September 2019. Two missions in Ukraine were carried out in November and December 2019 allowing the consultants to present the proposed approach to NEURC receive comments and meet key stakeholders representatives of different DSOs gas traders GTSO etc.. On this basis the consultant was able to continue the work and produced draft deliverables mainly covering the scope of work under the ToR e.g. review of existing metering and billing system in gas distribution review of metering and settlement regulations review the existing consumer categories and reference groups etc.. However starting March 2020 all missions were postponed due to COVID19 pandemic and only limited feedback and comments were received from NEURC until November 2020 with planned meetings being rescheduled due to unavailability of counterparts being on sick leave. The Draft Final Report was prepared by Algorus in August 2020 and delivered in November 2020 due to further absence of key NEURC members. Based on the comments and suggestions provided on the Report there was a need identified further continue the work and partially revise it to fully cover the request and comments presented by the Regulator. For this reason Phase 1 contract with Algorus was closed and considered to be accepted upon inviting a group of experts ready to follow up on methodological recommendations provided by Algorus and convert them into practical elements of daily balancing systems in DSOs. NEURC comments and additional demands were converted into new ToR and the new contract was signed September 2021. Part 2. The group of Ukrainian experts were hired to convert methodological recommendations provided by Algorus and turn them into technical consistent methodology for forecasting the daily consumption of natural gas in the absence of daily data transmission systems further work on mathematical apparatus taking into consideration available data from smart meters of available gas consumers. Considering the fact that the number of smart systems has been significantly increased during the past several years it was decided to update the statistics to further build the mathematical model then based on the proposed mathematical model and using received statistical data on daily consumption to form specify the profiles of consumption develop algorithms for adjusting consumption profiles during operation on the basis of operational dispatch data from smart systems of consumer control groups and determine the dependence of the necessary investments on the required forecasting error for each profile. The first draft of the report was delivered to NEURC at the end of October and fully accepted the final report is expected to be ready March 30 2022.The methodology for forecasting the daily gas consumption was improved considering i availability of daily data on gas consumption from smart meters and daily average air temperature ii significant contamination of input data irregular collection of information failure of meters etc. iii profiles iv the need to ensure the marginal level of forecasting error for 2 days within 10. It was also envisaged to use parametric submodels for forecasting time series data regression models and gradient boosting models and a complex of deep indepth learning models. Now the algorithm for forecasting daily level of natural gas consumption includes the following stages collection and generalization of primary data data cleaning and preparation for analysis and forecasting conducting evaluations of the effectiveness of forecasts based on neural networks selection of the best model based on the methodology forecast. NEURC accepted preliminary results finalization of teh report is ongoing

title.narrative: Support for reform of the Housing and Utilities Subsidy program, including Consumer Level monetization (CLM)

description.narrative: Support for reform of the Housing and Utilities Subsidy program, including Consumer Level monetization (CLM)

comment.narrative: Common Decision Protocol Settlement

The task is completed. The HUS reform remains a key priority in Ukraine in the face of high levels of energy poverty and continuing fiscal pressures. The team engaged successfully in a dialogue with the MoSP to implement changes to the eligibility conditions for improving targeting accuracy of the HUS. Additionally policy dialogue supported monetization of the HUS benefit for improved implementation transparency reduction of consumption and greater energy efficiency. WB provided just in time technical assistance by designing the overall concept for the flow of funds under the new monetized process the design architecture attached. HUS Program was monetized by the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine 1123 adopted on December 27th 2019. Overall there was significant change in HUS policy that was supported by the TF funded dialogue. This enabled private gas traders to compete with NG on gas supply to population improved incentives for EE and reduced potential for corruption.

title.narrative: Targeted dedicated support mechanisms for vulnerable consumers is developed

description.narrative: Targeted dedicated support mechanisms for vulnerable consumers is developed

comment.narrative: No specific mechanisms for vulnerable groups

The task supported the dialogue to improve targeting of the social assistance system that includes the HUS and GMI as part of feasibility of targeted support mechanisms for vulnerable energy consumers. In this context the WB analytics and conducted assessments to reduce reliance on the HUS and increase the role of GMI with the objective to reduce leakage of subsidies to nonpoor groups. This helped MoSP to develop the amendments to the HUS and GMI programs. Based on technical assistance from the WB the Ministry introduced additional eligibility conditions to eliminate nonpoor households from the program and improve energy efficiency incentives. In addition it implemented changes to the GMI program to increase support to vulnerable households. The Law 294IX on the State Budget for 2020 for the first time set the income threshold for the members of households who have lost the ability to work above the subsistence minimum at the level of 130 percent. Specific deliverables outputsAssessments of need and feasibility of targeted support mechanisms for vulnerable energy consumers i quantitative tool to estimate impact of energy price increase and parametric changes to the HUS to estimate poverty and fiscal impact. The excel based tool was shared with MoF and MoSP and guided their decision about midyear financing increase to the HUS ii technical assistance provided on improving targeting through advisory inputs and a report. Report attached and resulted in the change of the HUS threshold being moved from 15 percent to 20 percent of reference income iii technical econometric assessment of performance of HUS and simulation of further reform scenarios including discussion for improved energy efficiency. The report was published as a WB Working Paper for full public disclosure.
